description: Conversational learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway per card.

cards.title: Flavor Starts With Technique
cards.subtitle: Better cooking usually comes from basic technique, not rare ingredients.
body: Learning heat control, salting in layers, and proper timing changes everyday meals fast.
You do not need complicated recipes to cook well. You need repeatable fundamentals.
cards.takeaway: Master basics and meals improve immediately.

cards.title: Prep Reduces Weeknight Friction
cards.subtitle: Most bad food choices happen when time is short and energy is low.
body: Simple prep—washed greens, cooked grains, chopped aromatics—makes healthy meals easier than takeout when you are tired.
Cooking is less about motivation and more about reducing friction ahead of time.

cards.title: Recipes Are Maps, Not Laws
cards.subtitle: Following recipes exactly helps early, but adaptation is where skill grows.
body: Once you understand the role of acid, fat, salt, and heat, substitutions become intuitive.
Good cooks use recipes as scaffolding, then adjust for context and taste.

cards.title: Processed Food Optimizes for Craving
cards.subtitle: Many packaged foods are engineered for repeat consumption, not satiety.
body: High combinations of salt, sugar, and fat can override natural fullness signals.
Cooking more from whole ingredients restores control over flavor and nutrition.
cards.takeaway: What is convenient is not always neutral.

cards.title: Shared Meals Build More Than Nutrition
cards.subtitle: Cooking and eating together supports connection, not just calories.
body: Family and community meals create rhythms for conversation, belonging, and care.
Food is both fuel and social glue.
cards.takeaway: A meal can nourish relationships too.

cards.title: Kitchen Skills Are Economic Skills
cards.subtitle: Knowing how to cook lowers food costs while improving diet quality.
body: Small habits like batch cooking and using leftovers reduce waste and spending.
Cooking literacy is practical independence, especially when budgets are tight.
cards.takeaway: Skill in the kitchen creates options.

cards.title: Taste Preferences Are Trainable
cards.subtitle: You are not stuck with your current palate forever.
body: Repeated exposure can increase acceptance of bitter vegetables, less sugar, and new cuisines.
Preference often follows familiarity more than fixed identity.
cards.takeaway: What you practice tasting, you learn to enjoy.

cards.title: Good Cooking Is Iterative
cards.subtitle: Even experienced cooks miss textures and timings sometimes.
body: Treat each attempt as feedback: adjust heat, acid, salt, or timing next round.
Improvement comes from notes and repetition, not perfection on first try.
